content: There is no clearance for the bottom screws... Also these aligners do not guarantee alignment... bad bad bad step.
they should add a cutout for the bottom screw
even with the aligners you can still mount it incorrectly... There is nothing keeping the aligners parallel to each other
Yeah im almost 100% sure my working printer cant pass the x axis because of this one step

The alignment tool blocks the bottom screws on both sides - and it doesn't matter which tool is on which side.  I tightened the top two screws on each side then backed off the alignment tool and tightened the bottom screws on each side.

I'm starting to doubt if I should have started with this, but we'll see once the build is complete. But even with the "aligners" in place and tightly pushed against the frame, it's fairly easy to move each side in opposite direction relative to each other. So I'm not sure if this will result in better alignment.

replies.content: I tried to hold the alignment tool against the frame on each side as I tighten the screws. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

content: As others have commented, the lower screws are inaccessible with aligner on. Had to tighten the top ones first, then remove slingers, and tighten bottom screws.

Argh, I already hate myself for loosening the screws. Somehow I considered these steps necessary, but now my printer which had never any issues with the gantry might be in a worse condition. The aligners have too much play, it feels like I can do the job better by hand. And you even have to remove them to tighten the bottom screw.

replies.content: Same! This was a bad idea and now I doing this whole step a second time, after finishing the entire build and getting halfway through calibrations

content: why is this step necessary for converting an already assembled printer? It seems like I'm introducing potential errors into an already set up system.
The aliigner-tools could need a little cut-out for the lower screw on each side...

replies.content: The lower screws are just not reachable and need cutouts just as Pyron suggested.
